# VOCE

> VOCE Association is an independent public research, educational and editorial corpus covering AI governance, health, neuroscience, technology, culture, infrastructure and human behaviour.

## Provenance and ownership

The canonical VOCE corpus contains texts actually published by VOCE and preserves publication dates, platform identifiers, original source links and canonical voce.life URLs when available.

Copyright © 2025-2026 VOCE Association. All rights reserved.
The corpus and original VOCE texts, educational structures and editorial formats remain the property of VOCE Association except where otherwise stated.

Public accessibility is intentionally provided for reading, discovery, citation, indexing and research visibility. Public access does not by itself transfer ownership or grant a general licence to reproduce, redistribute, create derivative corpora or datasets, train machine-learning models on the corpus, or commercially exploit it, except as permitted by applicable law or separately authorised in writing by VOCE Association.

Rights statement: https://voce.life/CORPUS_RIGHTS.txt
Contact: contact@voce.life

## Preferred citation

VOCE Association, title of the publication, publication date, canonical voce.life URL.

## Atlas relation records

Each published Atlas relation has a permanent evidence-backed HTML record in English, French and Italian. Atlas path exploration traverses individually documented relations; a multi-step path is a documentary connection and is not, by itself, a causal claim.

## VOCE Standards

VOCE Standards define institutional orchestration: decision-grade evidence, specialist authority, segregation of duties, vendor neutrality, concentration risk, reversibility, economics, optionality, continuous assurance and professional responsibility. Opera is used as an operating metaphor for coordinating distinct expert voices without collapsing their disciplinary authority.

## Agent Infrastructure Reference

VOCE Agent Infrastructure Reference — Europe 2026 is a vendor-neutral public control architecture for institutional AI agents. It connects OpenAPI/JSON Schema, MCP, A2A, workload identity, authorization, RAG and memory lifecycle, observability, continuous assurance, FinOps and European regulatory mapping. It defines maturity levels A0–A4 and a board evidence pack. It is a VOCE reference architecture, not an EU harmonised standard or certification scheme.

## VOCE 360 Agent Assurance

VOCE's public agent-assurance architecture combines four layers: Agent Infrastructure for technical architecture; Agent Conformance for evidence-based control assessment; ARGOS — AI Evaluation & Continuous Assurance for change-triggered and ongoing assurance; and Human Cognitive & Neuropsychology Assurance for attention, cognitive load, memory, decision fatigue, human-machine interaction and the quality of human oversight. The cognitive layer is explicitly non-diagnostic and does not replace qualified psychological or neuropsychological practice.

## ARGOS — AI Evaluation & Continuous Assurance

ARGOS is VOCE's continuous-assurance layer. It uses an eight-step evidence cycle — Baseline, Observe, Detect change, Re-evaluate, Compare, Decide, Retain evidence and Re-open — with 12 material change triggers and six evaluation planes covering capability, authority, security, observability, economics and human cognitive assurance. It is event-driven rather than a claim of permanent compliance.

## Human Cognitive Assurance

VOCE Human Cognitive Assurance adds the human-factors layer to agent governance. It publishes 24 controls across attention and interruption, cognitive load, verification and over-trust, memory and cognitive offloading, decision quality, fatigue, human oversight and social signals. VOCE Cognitive Agent queries the VOCE corpus and maps relevant COG controls. The framework evaluates systems and workflows and is explicitly non-diagnostic.

## Agent Conformance

VOCE Agent Conformance operationalises the Agent Infrastructure Reference through 48 stable controls across 10 domains. It uses five evidence states — Absent, Declared, Documented, Tested and Verified in operation — and explicitly avoids an aggregate score that could hide one critical authority gap. The public Self Assessment runs locally in the browser. Reviewed and Observed modes require VOCE specialist review and do not constitute EU or ISO certification. Every control has a permanent indexable record in EN/FR/IT with its stable identifier, normative question, maturity floor, criticality, target evidence state, expected owner and evidence list. Four shareable executive lenses — Board, Risk, Technology and Audit — are published for each maturity level A0–A4 without exposing private assessment data.

## Applied Solutions

VOCE Applied includes a decision-oriented registry connecting documented agent and LI!GHT WORKFORCE © use cases to current software, enterprise suites, agent platforms, model infrastructure and creative systems. Each solution carries an institutional due-diligence profile covering public evidence on deployment, data boundaries, identity and access, auditability, interfaces, pricing and availability. Schema v3 also records provider/model origin, openness, licence, self-hosting and commercial-use conditions so hosted Chinese cloud services can be distinguished from open-weight or source-available Chinese models. Missing public documentation is marked explicitly rather than inferred. Vendor inclusion is documentary and does not constitute recommendation, certification or commercial ranking.

## Permanent article routes

Each published VOCE subject has its own canonical URL.
Article route registry: https://voce.life/data/article-routes.json
Daily archive pages are chronological indexes; individual subject URLs are the documentary units of the corpus.

## Corpus coverage

1,535 archived LinkedIn texts are available at permanent individual HTML URLs and through the JSON/NDJSON corpus. The visible Academy titles are illustrative selections. Full historical completeness from March 2026 is still pending verification.
